test_title: PYST 3: SSC Stenographer - English (Held On:12 Oct, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
**Select the option that changes the form of narration in the following sentence.**

The priest said to the convict, “Are you not ashamed of your misdeed?

options.text: The priest enquired the convict of whether she is not ashamed of her misdeed.
The priest enquired of the convict if she was not ashamed of her misdeed.
The priest enquired of the convict that she was not ashamed of her misdeed.
The priest enquired of the convict if was she not ashamed of her misdeed.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option (2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the reporting verb has **an object** ('the convict'), and the nature of the sentence is **interrogative (question form)**.
 
• **'Said to' **in an interrogative sentence will often change into **'enquired of' or 'asked'** when reporting the question in indirect speech.
 
• **Comma (,) **and **inverted commas ("...") **will be **removed** in indirect speech.
 
• The conjunction **'if'** or** 'whether'** is typically added to introduce reported yes-no questions in indirect speech.
 
• Pronouns change according to the object of the reported speech. Here, it implies **'the convict'** is a female **because no option__ consists of ‘he’. **
 
• **'Are' **in the direct speech becomes** 'was' **to keep the tense consistency in reported speech, reflecting a shift from direct to indirect narration.

**Therefore, the correct answer is *"The priest enquired of the convict if she was not ashamed of her misdeed."***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Let’s identify the reporting speech and reported speech.

 
 
• He said, “I go to school every day.”
 
• In the above sentence “He said” is the reporting speech.
 
• “I go to school every day.” is the reported speech.
